newsitem.title: GERMANY: Degussa says upbeat for 1996/97 year.
newsitem.headline: Degussa says upbeat for 1996/97 year.

text.p: German chemicals and metals group Degussa AG said on Monday it expected its business to continue developing well in the 1996/97 year to September 30 after reporting a two percent rise in pre-tax profit in 1995/1996.
The current business year had started well and the marked improvement in business in recent months, particularly in Europe, was likely to continue, Degussa said in a statement.
Degussa said it expected a "continued positive development" in 1996/1997.
Degussa said pre-tax profit rose two percent to a record 413 million marks in the 1995/96 year ended September and that earnings per share advanced to 39 marks from 38.

The company reported its 1995/96 results based on a reorganised management structure with the three divisions chemical products, health and nutrition, and precious metals and bank activities. Year-earlier results have been made comparable.
Adjusted for changes in the consolidated group and in precious metals trading, group sales fell two percent, Degussa said.
Group sales in the 1995/96 year fell one percent to 13.79 billion marks, with a fall in sales in Germany being offset by slight gains elsewhere in Europe.
Sales in North America and Latin America rose markedly, Degussa said.
